youtube_description:
In a recent study published in the journal Nature, astronomers report the discovery of the largest explosion ever observed in the universe. The explosion, dubbed AT2021lwx, was ten times brighter than any known supernova and has been raging for at least three years.

AT2021lwx is located about 8 billion light-years from Earth and thus occurred when the universe was just 6 billion years old. The cause of the explosion is still unknown, but it is possible that it was caused by the merger of two neutron stars or the collision of a star with a supermassive black hole.

The discovery of AT2021lwx is a major breakthrough in astronomy and provides new insights into the extreme events that can occur in the universe. The study also raises new questions about the nature of these explosions and their role in the evolution of the universe.
